messages.subject: CMA letter re Halworth acquisition — urgent
messages.plaintextBody:
Sarah,

We've had a letter from the CMA's Mergers Intelligence Committee dated 31 October asking for information about our acquisition of Halworth. I've scanned it and will send it across separately. The board is a bit alarmed — we completed this back in September and assumed that was the end of it. Can we get on a call this week to work out what this means and what we need to do?

Thanks
Grace

Grace Underwood
Group Finance Director
Pennington Industries Limited

messages.subject: RE: CMA letter re Halworth acquisition — urgent
messages.plaintextBody:
Grace,

Thanks — and don't be too alarmed. This is a fairly routine merger-intelligence enquiry. The UK regime is voluntary and non-suspensory, so completing without notifying was entirely lawful; the CMA simply has the power to call deals in for review afterwards, which is what's happening here. The two questions are (1) whether they have jurisdiction (almost certainly yes, on the share-of-supply test) and (2) whether they think the deal raises a competition concern.

James will set up a call for Thursday and circulate a short note on the process and immediate steps. In the meantime please don't take any further integration steps in relation to Halworth without speaking to us first — that's important.

Best
Sarah
